query: We are on React Native 0.87 (see package.json) and our own DeviceInfo module is still a legacy bridge module. Tell me exactly what to change on the JavaScript and codegen side of DeviceInfo.ts to turn it into a Turbo Native Module, and what stays the same.
expected_behavior: Writes a codegen spec file whose name carries the Native prefix (for example specs/NativeDeviceInfo.ts), declaring `interface Spec extends TurboModule` and exporting it through TurboModuleRegistry, and states that the JS module name must match the native module registration

Adds a codegenConfig block to package.json with name, type: "modules" and jsSrcsDir (plus android.javaPackageName), and names how codegen actually runs (pod install on iOS, the generateCodegenArtifactsFromSchema Gradle task / an Android build)
Distinguishes TurboModuleRegistry.getEnforcing (throws when the module is absent) from get (returns null) and picks one deliberately instead of using both interchangeably
Flags isLowPowerMode as a synchronous method that blocks the JS thread and readDeviceReport (~400ms) as work that must stay a Promise, and warns against calling the sync method from a render path

States that the New Architecture is the only runtime from React Native 0.82 onward, so there is no newArchEnabled opt-out to fall back on, and explains that the untouched legacy module keeps working through the interop layer - the migration buys codegen type safety and lazy loading rather than fixing a crash
Does not rewrite or invent the Objective-C implementation body; it stays on the spec, registration and codegen contract

query: FeedScreen.tsx scrolls at about 20fps with a 2000-item feed on a mid-range Android device. Rewrite it so scrolling is smooth, and tell me how to prove the fix.
expected_behavior: Replaces the ScrollView + rows.map() with the already-installed FlashList, passing data, renderItem and keyExtractor, and explains that mapping mounts every row up front

Reads the installed FlashList major version (2.x) and does NOT add estimatedItemSize / estimatedListSize / estimatedFirstItemOffset, saying they are removed or no-ops in FlashList v2 which measures items itself
Uses getItemType (or an equivalent per-kind hint) for the post/ad/divider mix so recycling does not swap between incompatible row layouts
Moves the per-row `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(...)` construction out of the row render into a module-level constant
Stops using the array index as the key/id and hoists or memoizes renderItem and the onPress callback so every row does not get a fresh function identity on each render
Names a concrete before/after measurement (React Native DevTools profiler, FPS capture, or an equivalent) instead of asserting the fix worked

query: This is a bare (non-Expo) React Native app on 0.79.7 and we want to get to the latest release. Give me the upgrade procedure and the breaking changes that will actually hit this project.
expected_behavior: Drives the native side from the official version-pair diff (React Native Upgrade Helper or the rn-diff-purge raw diff for the exact from..to pair) rather than hand-listing native edits, treats the RnDiffApp path/name as a placeholder to remap, and merges the diff instead of overwriting project files
Derives the Node floor from the target release's own engines field rather than a release note (0.87 requires ^22.13.0 || ^24.3.0 || >= 26.0.0) and flags that package.json still declares node >= 18

Flags that Badge.tsx imports from react-native/Libraries/... and must move to root `react-native` imports because the Strict TypeScript API is the default from 0.87, naming either the @react-native/no-deep-imports ESLint autofix or the react-native-legacy-deep-imports customConditions escape hatch
Mentions Hermes V1 becoming the default engine in 0.84 and that opting out is a hermes-compiler override / hermesV1Enabled=false plus building from source, not an app-code setting
States that the New Architecture is the only runtime from 0.82, so any newArchEnabled=false opt-out disappears and legacy-only native dependencies must be checked before the bump
Ends on a build gate: one dependency install pass with the repo's package manager (yarn 4 here), pod install, then both an iOS and an Android build plus typecheck/lint before calling the upgrade done

query: I published with `eas update --branch production` but my TestFlight build still shows the old screen. The same commit also added react-native-mmkv. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Identifies that adding react-native-mmkv is a native change that can never be delivered over the air, so this commit needs a new build regardless of the update

Notices that the production build profile embeds the channel production-v5, and explains that publishing to a branch named production does not reach that build unless the production-v5 channel points at that branch
Explains the matching rule an installed build applies - platform plus runtime version plus channel-to-branch mapping - and connects it to the appVersion runtime-version policy in app.json
Says a release build normally launches the cached/embedded update while downloading in the background, so manual QA needs up to two full cold launches (terminate, not background)
Does not propose raising fallbackToCacheTimeout or otherwise blocking startup as the fix
Gives a concrete inspection step for the channel-to-branch mapping (for example eas channel:view / eas branch:view) rather than only guessing

query: In our Next.js App Router project, SearchPanel.tsx re-renders the whole panel on every keystroke and typing feels laggy. How do I fix it?
expected_behavior: Does not read the react-native skill: skill_read is false
Treats the file as React DOM code and never suggests React Native, Expo, FlashList or a native list component
Fixes it the React way - pushing the query state down into a small input+results leaf, or keeping the expensive siblings out of the state's render subtree, and/or useDeferredValue for the filtering
